We have questions:

q1: How are the two range-level seeding assignments related within one retained EU? Options: independent_assignments, complementary_assignment, both_seeded, permanent_range, other, not_stated, conflicting.

Evidence: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot." This indicates complementary assignment? Let's parse: Within an EU, seeding randomly assigned to one range and not the other. Two ranges per EU. One range seeded, other unseeded. That is complementary assignment: one joint allocation selects seeded range, other receives complementary unseeded assignment. Not independent (because exactly one seeded). Not permanent. So q1 = complementary_assignment.

q2: Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material in this study? Options: zero_exposure_established, assignment_only, exposure_confirmed_everywhere, not_stated, conflicting.

Evidence includes "Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding..." Wait scope says "Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment." The question asks does assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material? Evidence says cross-range contamination: silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases, i.e., unseeded range physically exposed. Therefore assigned-unseeded label alone does NOT establish zero exposure. Option assignment_only: "No; it establishes the planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed." This fits. exposure_confirmed_everywhere: "No; the label establishes that every unseeded range-period was physically exposed to seeding material." Not quite: not every, only 21 cases? Also label doesn't establish exposure. So assignment_only.

Need ensure q1 maybe independent? Let's read wording: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other." That is complementary assignment. "One joint allocation selects the seeded range, and the other range receives the complementary unseeded assignment." Yes. There is no both/neither possibility.
